cases.note: The kitāb's opening definition (ḥadd) of ṭahāra, not a ruling (ḥukm) on a case. Examined: advance_after_cause (qāʿida 4: ḥadath as the sabab of ṭahāra's wujūb), which presupposes this definition but does not state it. ʿUmda opens with the waters and gives no definition.
cases.quote: وهي ارتفاع الحدث وما في معناه وزوال الخبث
cases.expected: Ṭahāra is the lifting of ḥadath and what is in its meaning, and the removal of khabath (impurity).

cases.note: Leading ruling: only ṭahūr water (طهور) lifts ḥadath and removes najas; the tripartite division (ṭahūr, ṭāhir, najis) opens it. A domain rule of the waters; running_water (qāʿida 1) only measures a running body and does not decide which liquids purify.
cases.quote: لا يرفع الحدث ولا يزيل النجس الطارئ غيره
cases.expected: Waters are three; only ṭahūr water, the water remaining as created, lifts ḥadath and removes supervening najas.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: «فلا تحصل الطهارة بمائع غيره»; agrees. ʿUmda divides the waters by whether they become najis, not into three kinds.

cases.note: Leading ruling: change by a non-mixing (غير ممازج) thing leaves the water ṭahūr with karāha. istihlak (qāʿida 22) is about a thing consumed in the water without trace, not a non-mixing thing whose trace shows, so it does not decide. Heating by najis fuel (karāha) is a second ruling of the same domain.
cases.quote: فإن تغير بغير ممازج كقطع كافور ودهن أو بملح مائي أوسخن بنجس كره
cases.expected: Water changed by a non-mixing thing (lumps of camphor, oil), by sea salt, or heated by najis fuel is ṭahūr but disliked (makrūh).

aligned.note: ʿUmda treats only a mixing (خالطه) pure thing, which removes ṭahūriyya when it overcomes the water's name; the non-mixing case is not stated there.

cases.note: Leading ruling: change by standing or by what is hard to keep from the water (ما يشق صون الماء عنه) does not even make it makrūh. Examined: unknown_as_nonexistent, whose hardship fact is about an unknown thing treated as absent, not about an unavoidable admixture; no reading states the hardship (mashaqqa) exemption for water.
cases.quote: وإن تغير بمكثه أو بما يشق صون الماء عنه من نابت فيه أو ورق1 شجر أو بمجاورة ميتة أو سخن بالشمس أو بطاهر لم يكره
cases.expected: Water changed by standing, by what is hard to keep from it (plants, leaves), by an adjacent carcass, or heated by the sun or a pure fuel, is ṭahūr and not disliked.

aligned.note: ʿUmda states the opposite case (a mixing pure thing overcoming the name removes ṭahūriyya); the exemption is not stated there.

cases.note: Leading ruling: water used (mustaʿmal) in a recommended ṭahāra stays ṭahūr with karāha. Examined: excess_over_sufficient (qāʿida 3), which decides whether a washing (ghasl) beyond the obligatory (wājib) one is itself obligatory, not the status of the water it used.
cases.quote: وإن استعمل في طهارة مستحبة كتجديد وضوء وغسل جمعة "وغسلة ثانية وثالثة" كره
cases.expected: Water used in a recommended ṭahāra (renewing wuḍūʾ, Friday ghusl, the second and third washing) is ṭahūr but disliked.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: water used in lifting ḥadath (رفع حدث) loses ṭahūriyya; used water in a recommended ṭahāra is not stated there.

cases.note: Leading ruling: much water (two qullas, «وهو الكثير») with a najāsa other than human urine or liquid excrement that does not change it is ṭahūr. The najāsa is consumed without trace («فلم تغيره») and treated as absent; Ibn Rajab q022.f000: «فإن كان كثيرا سقط حكمها بغير خلاف». The quantity, the fact q022.f000 lacked, is stated here. Not the whole unit: the human-urine branch (najis unless hard to drain) departs from the reading; al-Inṣāf (v01:p059) calls not becoming najis «أصح» and «قلت: وهذا المذهب على ما اصطلحناه», the other being «المذهب عند أكثر المتقدمين». That branch is a riwāya choice, outside the leading ruling.
cases.quote: فخالطته نجاسة غير بول آدمي أو عذرته المائعة فلم تغيره أو خالطه البول أو العذرة ويشق نزحه "كمصانع طريق مكة" فطهور

aligned.note: Zād states the much-water branch on which Ibn Rajab reports no khilāf.
ʿUmda: «فإذا بلغ الماء قلتين أو كان جاريا لم ينجسه شيء إلا ما غير لونه أو طعمه أو ريحه». Agree on the leading ruling; they disagree on human urine and excrement, which ʿUmda does not except.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the man may not lift his ḥadath with a little water a woman was alone with (خلت به) for a complete ṭahāra. A text-based (taʿabbudī) domain rule of the waters; no reading decides it. Not in ʿUmda; no Ibn Rajab farʿ found.
cases.quote: ولا يرفع "حدث" رجل طهور "يسير" خلت به امرأة لطهارة "كاملة عن حدث"
cases.expected: A little ṭahūr water a woman used alone for a complete ṭahāra from ḥadath does not lift a man's ḥadath.

cases.note: Leading ruling: water changed in taste, colour or smell by a pure thing cooked or fallen in becomes ṭāhir (not ṭahūr). The sentence's predicate «فطاهر» and its further subjects (a little water used to lift ḥadath, a hand dipped after night sleep, the last washing (ghasl) that removed najāsa) are printed in the next record (p09, a page-break continuation). Not istihlak: the trace shows, and the question is whether a changed water is still unqualified water, a domain rule.
cases.quote: وإن تغير طعمه أو لونه2 أو ريحه بطبخ أو ساقط فيه
cases.expected: Water whose taste, colour or smell changed by cooking or by something falling in, or of which a little was used to lift ḥadath, … is ṭāhir (pure, not purifying).

positions.ruling: Any change of taste, colour or smell by a pure thing falling in makes the water ṭāhir.
A mixing pure thing removes ṭahūriyya only when it overcomes the water's name («فغلب على اسمه»).

aligned.note: ʿUmda: cooking and use in lifting ḥadath remove ṭahūriyya (agree); a mixing pure thing does so only «فغلب على اسمه», where Zād rules ṭāhir on any change of taste, colour or smell: they disagree on mixing.

cases.note: Second half of the sentence begun in p08, split at a page break (audit page_break_candidates): it opens «حدث» completing «أو رفع بقليله» and carries the predicate «فطاهر». Its subjects (a little water used to lift ḥadath; a hand of one rising from night sleep dipped in it; the last washing (ghasl) that removed najāsa) are named in p08's note.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: water used in lifting ḥadath loses ṭahūriyya.

cases.note: Leading ruling: water changed by najāsa is najis. The najāsa's trace shows, so it is not consumed and not treated as absent (istihlak false): its ruling stands. Not the whole unit: the second ruling, a little water that met najāsa without change is najis, is the little-water branch of q022.f000 («وإن كان يسيرا فروايتان»), on which the reading takes the other side; the third (what separated from a place before its najāsa was removed) is a domain rule of washing (ghasl).
cases.quote: والنجس: ما تغير بنجاسة

aligned.note: The changed water, where no one holds the najāsa consumed.
ʿUmda: «إلا ما غير لونه أو طعمه أو ريحه وما عدا ذلك ينجس بمخالطة النجاسة»; agrees on the changed and on the little water.

cases.note: Leading ruling: adding much ṭahūr water (other than earth and the like) purifies najis water. istihlak would decide it (the najāsa consumed in much water is treated as absent), but the text does not state that the change is gone after the addition, only for the second and third routes («زال تغير النجس الكثير بنفسه», «فبقي بعده كثير»). The manner of adding (customary continuity) is q103.f001.
cases.quote: فإن أضيف إلى الماء النجس طهور كثير
cases.expected: Najis water becomes pure when much ṭahūr water is added to it, when the change of much najis water ceases of itself, or when what remains after draining is much and unchanged.

aligned.note: Ibn Rajab: the addition (mukāthara) needs only customary continuity, not two qullas poured at once.

cases.note: Doubt in the najāsa or the ṭahāra of water or anything else: build on certainty. On the facts of q159.f007 (known state, no amāra for its removal), the ẓāhir does not prevail over the aṣl. The whole unit.
cases.quote: وإن شك في نجاسة ماء "أو غيره" أو طهارته بنى على اليقين

aligned.note: ʿUmda's leading ruling: «وإذا شك في طهارة الماء أو غيره أو نجاسته بني على اليقين»; agree.

cases.note: Leading ruling: ṭahūr water confused with najis: both are forbidden and he does not seek the likelier (لم يتحر), as q109.f006 «يمنع من الطهارة بواحدة منها حتى يتبين». Not the whole unit: neither pouring out nor mixing is a condition (sharṭ) of tayammum; ṭahūr confused with ṭāhir: one wuḍūʾ, a handful from each, and one prayer (rule:confused_tahur_with_tahir). Using one and finding it ṭāhir is q068.f002.
cases.quote: وإن اشتبه طهور بنجس "حرم استعمالهما" ولم يتحر

aligned.note: Wuḍūʾ from a confused vessel later found ṭāhir: not valid «في المشهور».
A report that a dog licked one of two vessels: «صار كمن اشتبه عليه طاهر بنجس».
ʿUmda: «وإن اشتبه ماء طهور بنجس ولم يجد غيرهما تيمم وتركهما وإن اشتبه طهور بطاهر توضأ من كل واحد منهما»; agree on both branches.

cases.note: Leading ruling: repeat the prayer, one per najis garment plus one, until certain of one in a ṭāhir garment. vague_one_bars_all bars using any of the confused, which would leave him without a garment; the text instead requires repetition to certainty, a rule no reading states.
cases.quote: وإن اشتبهت ثياب طاهرة بنجسة "أو بمحرمة" صلى في كل ثوب صلاة بعدد النجس1 وزاد صلاة
cases.expected: Pure garments confused with najis (or forbidden) ones: he prays in each garment, as many prayers as the najis ones plus one.

aligned.note: A report of the najāsa of one of two garments is accepted as a confusion.
ʿUmda: «وإن اشتبهت ثياب طاهرة بنجسة صلى في كل ثوب بعدد النجس وزاد صلاة»; agree.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the permission of every pure vessel. Its exception, the prohibition of gold and silver vessels, is a domain rule from the ḥadīth. The third ruling, «وتصح الطهارة منها», is what prohibited_worship decides on target outside (the prohibition bears on the vessel, outside the ṭahāra): valid. Its next ruling, «وتكره», continues in p02 (page break).
cases.quote: كل إناء طاهر ولو ثمينا يباح اتخاذه واستعماله
cases.expected: Every pure vessel, even precious, may be acquired and used, except vessels of gold and silver and those plated with them, forbidden to acquire and use even for a woman; ṭahāra from them is valid; a small silver plate for need is excepted.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: «ويجوز استعمال سائر الآنية الطاهر واتخاذها»; agree.
ʿUmda: gold and silver vessels forbidden «في طهارة ولا غيرها», the plated alike except a small silver plate; agree. ʿUmda does not state acquisition, women, or the validity of the ṭahāra.

cases.note: Second half of the sentence of p01 split at a page break (audit page_break_candidates): «مباشرتها» completes the «وتكره» of p01 (touching the small silver plate without need is disliked).

Leading ruling: vessels and clothes of unbelievers, even those whose slaughter is not lawful, are permitted when their state is unknown: the aṣl of ṭahāra against the ẓāhir of contamination, the question of q159.f025, on its facts. Zād holds riwāya 1 (the aṣl); the reading lands on riwāya 3 («إن قوي الظاهر جدا لم يجز استعمالها بدون غسل»). al-Inṣāf: riwāya 1 is «المذهب مطلقا»: off the reading's side; ledger entry. Further rulings: tanned carrion skin is not purified (q134.f002, as prevention_easier_than_removal has it), its use in dry things from an animal pure in life is permitted (q085.f012), carrion bones, milk and parts are najis except hair (q002.f001, hair_detached), and what is cut from the living is as its carrion (rule:severed_part_as_carrion).
cases.quote: وتباح آنية الكفار ولو لم تحل ذبائحهم وثيابهم إن جهل حالها

positions.who: riwāya 1, the madhhab per al-Inṣāf; Zād
riwāya 2: disliked (makrūh) for fear of contamination
riwāya 3: if the ẓāhir is very strong, not used before washing (ghasl)

aligned.note: Tanning after death does not purify «على ظاهر المذهب»; Zād: «ولا يطهر جلد ميتة بدباغ».
Tanned skin used in dry things.
Hair is not made najis by death; Zād: «غير شعر ونحوه».

ʿUmda: «واستعمال أواني أهل الكتاب وثيابهم ما لم تعلم نجاستها» (the People of the Book, a sub-case of Zād's unbelievers); agree. Also agree: «وكل جلد ميتة دبغ أو لم يدبغ فهو نجس», hair pure, bones najis.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the recommended (mustaḥabb, «يستحب») formula on entering the privy; then the formula on leaving, the left foot first in and the right out, leaning on the left foot, distance and screening in open land, a soft spot for urine, wiping and shaking the penis thrice, moving away to wash (ghasl) if fearing to be soiled. Manners of relieving oneself (ādāb) are domain rules; command_prophetic_act_usage would only grade a reported act, which Zād does not cite.
cases.quote: يستحب عند دخول الخلاء قول: بسم الله أعوذ بالله من الخبث والخبائث
cases.expected: On entering the privy it is recommended to say the basmala and the taʿawwudh, and on leaving «غفرانك …», with the further recommended manners listed.

aligned.note: ʿUmda gives the same formulas (adding «ومن الرجس النجس الشيطان الرجيم»); agree.
ʿUmda: the feet, leaning on the left foot, distance, screening, a soft spot, wiping and shaking thrice; agree. Zād adds moving away «إن خاف تلوثا».

cases.note: Leading ruling: karāha of entering with something bearing God's name, unless for need. The other makrūhāt of the list follow. Domain rules of the privy; amr reads a command's force, and no command is cited.
cases.quote: ويكره دخوله بشيء فيه ذكر الله تعالى إلا لحاجة
cases.expected: It is disliked to enter with something bearing God's name except for need, to raise the garment before nearing the ground, to speak in it, to urinate in a crack, to touch the penis or wipe with the right hand, and to face the sun or moon.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: «ولا يدخله بشيء فيه ذكر الله تعالى إلا من حاجة», «ولا يبولن في ثقب ولا شق», «ولا يمس ذكره بيمينه ولا يتمسح بها», «ولا يستقبل شمسا ولا قمرا». Agree on the acts; ʿUmda states them as prohibitions without grading karāha from taḥrīm.

cases.note: Leading ruling: taḥrīm of facing or turning one's back to the qibla outside buildings. The building exception is the specification (takhṣīṣ) of the general prohibition by a report, a domain rule; amr does not decide where the prohibition holds.
cases.quote: ويحرم استقبال القبلة واستدبارها في غير بنيان1
cases.expected: Facing or turning one's back to the qibla is forbidden outside buildings, as are lingering beyond need and urinating in a road, useful shade, or under a fruiting tree.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: «ولا يستقبل القبلة ولا يستدبرها … ويجوز ذلك في البنيان», «ولا يبولن في … طريق ولا ظل نافع ولا تحت شجرة مثمرة»; agree.

cases.note: Leading ruling: stones then water, and stones alone suffice unless the exit passed its usual place. Examined: combining_forms (qāʿida 12: whether to combine two ways of an act); here combining is the better way and either suffices, by the domain rule of istinjāʾ.
cases.quote: ويستجمر3 ثم يستنجي بالماء وبجزئه الاستجمار إن لم يعد الخارج موضع العادة
cases.expected: He wipes with stones, then washes with water; stones alone suffice if what exited did not pass its usual place.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: «ثم يستجمر وترا ثم يستنجي بالماء وإن اقتصر على الاستجمار أجزأه إذا لم تتعد النجاسة موضع العادة»; agree.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the conditions (sharṭ, «ويشترط») of the means of istijmār, first ṭahāra and cleansing. A domain rule. The excluded bone, dung and revered things are what prohibited_worship would decide (a prohibition on the means as a specific condition: no sufficiency), but the text gives them as conditions, not prohibitions.
cases.quote: ويشترط لاستجمار4 بأحجار ونحوها: أن يكون طاهرا5 منقيا
cases.expected: Stones and the like for istijmār must be pure, cleansing, and not bone, dung, food, a revered thing, or attached to an animal.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: «ويجوز الاستجمار بكل طاهر إلا الروث والعظام وما له حرمة»; agree. ʿUmda does not name food or what is attached to an animal.

cases.note: Leading ruling: at least three cleansing wipes. A number fixed by the ḥadīth, a domain rule; excess_over_sufficient (qāʿida 3) concerns what is beyond the required, not the required number.
cases.quote: ويشترط ثلاث مسحات منقية فأكثر ولو بحجر ذي شعب
cases.expected: Three cleansing wipes or more are required, even with one stone of several faces.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: «ولا يجزئ أقل من ثلاث مسحات منقيه»; agree. Zād adds the stone of several faces.

cases.note: A sunna of istijmār; domain rule.
cases.quote: ويسن قطعه على وتر
cases.expected: It is sunna to end the wiping on an odd number.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: «ثم يستجمر وترا»; agree.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the wujūb («ويجب») of istinjāʾ for every exit but wind. The second ruling, that wuḍūʾ before it is not valid («ولا يصح»), is the order of the two ṭahāras; advance_after_cause (qāʿida 4) allows advancing an act after its sabab, which does not decide whether one ṭahāra must precede another. Not stated in ʿUmda.
cases.quote: ويجب الاستنجاء لكل خارج إلا الريح ولا يصح قبله وضوء ولا تيمم
cases.expected: Istinjāʾ is obligatory for every exit except wind; neither wuḍūʾ nor tayammum is valid before it.

cases.note: Leading ruling: siwāk is sunna at all times but for the faster after noon (al-zawāl). Zād cites no command; command_obligation_status would read «لولا أن أشق على أمتي لأمرتهم», which ʿUmda cites, as not obligatory, but the faster's exception and the times are domain rules.
cases.quote: التسوك بعود لين منق غير مضر لا يتفتت لا بإصبعه وخرقة مسنون كل وقت لغير صائم بعد الزوال
cases.expected: Siwāk with a soft, cleansing, harmless stick that does not crumble (not a finger or cloth) is sunna at all times, except for a fasting person after noon, and stressed at prayer, waking and change of the mouth.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: «ويسن السواك عند تغير الفم والقيام من النوم وعند الصلاة … ويستحب في سائر الأوقات إلا للصائم بعد الزوال»; agree. ʿUmda does not exclude the finger or cloth.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the manner of siwāk; oiling every other day (غبا) follows. Domain rules of grooming (sunan al-fiṭra). Not in ʿUmda.
cases.quote: ويستاك عرضا مبتدئا بجانب فمه الأيمن
cases.expected: He uses the siwāk across the teeth, beginning with the right side of the mouth; and oils himself every other day.

cases.note: A grooming sunna. The audit lists this record as a page-break candidate (p02 ends «غبا,»), but it opens its own verb and ruling, so it is a masʾala. Not in ʿUmda.
cases.quote: ويكتحل وترا
cases.expected: He applies kohl an odd number of times.

cases.note: Leading ruling: tasmiya is wājib, falling with forgetting («مع الذكر»). Its obligation is a riwāya choice on the ḥadīth denying wuḍūʾ to one who does not mention the name of God, which no reading decides; excused_error would only excuse the forgetter. ʿUmda lists the tasmiya among the sunan: the two mutūn disagree. al-Inṣāf (v01, on «وسنن الوضوء … والتسمية»): «وعنه أنها واجبة وهي المذهب», and the sunna riwāya «واختارها الخرقي، وابن أبي موسى، والمصنف». Not ledgered: no reading expresses the dispute.
cases.quote: ويجب التسمية في الوضوء مع الذكر
cases.expected: The basmala (tasmiya) in wuḍūʾ is obligatory when one remembers it.

positions.who: Zād; the riwāya al-Inṣāf calls the madhhab
ʿUmda; the riwāya chosen by al-Khiraqī and Ibn Qudāma

aligned.note: ʿUmda: «والمسنون التسمية»; disagree (Zād: wājib).

cases.note: Leading ruling: khitān is wājib, lapsing with fear for oneself. Examined: substitute (inability lifts the original to a substitute); here fear lifts the obligation with no substitute, a domain rule. Not in ʿUmda.
cases.quote: ويجب الختان ما لم يخف على نفسه
cases.expected: Circumcision is obligatory unless he fears for himself; qazaʿ (shaving part of the head) is disliked.

cases.note: Leading ruling: siwāk is a sunna of wuḍūʾ; the list follows. Washing (ghasl) the hands after night sleep is made wājib, a riwāya choice. «وأخذ ماء جديد للأذنين» is one of the two ways q012.f000 gives for wiping the ears, which combining_forms decides is not to be combined; Zād states only that way, so the reading does not decide the leading ruling.
cases.quote: ومن سنن الوضوء السواك
cases.expected: Among the sunan of wuḍūʾ: siwāk, washing the hands thrice (obligatory after night sleep), beginning with rinsing the mouth then the nose, thoroughness in both except for the faster, combing the thick beard and the fingers, starting with the right, new water for the ears, and the second and third washing.

aligned.note: ʿUmda lists the same sunan (hands, thoroughness except for the faster, combing beard and fingers, right before left, thrice); agree. ʿUmda b00004.p02 excepts the hands from the obligatory without distinguishing night sleep, where Zād makes the washing wājib: they differ on that branch.
Ears wiped once, with the head or with new water.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the six furūḍ of wuḍūʾ, a domain enumeration. Its measure of muwālāt by the drying of the limbs is one of the two riwāyas of q103.f002 («بالعرف أو بجفاف الأعضاء»); continuity decides only that a slight gap does not break it.
cases.quote: فروضه ستة
cases.expected: Wuḍūʾ has six obligatory acts: washing the face (with mouth and nose), the arms, wiping the head (with the ears), washing the feet, order (tartīb) and continuity (muwālāt), which is not delaying a limb until the previous one dries.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: «والواجب من ذلك النية والغسل مرة مرة ما خلا الكفين ومسح الرأس كله وترتيب الوضوء … وأن لا يؤخر غسل عضو حتى ينشف ما قبله»; agree (ʿUmda counts the intention among them, Zād makes it a condition in p02).
The measure of muwālāt; Zād takes the drying of the limbs.

cases.note: Leading ruling: niyya is a sharṭ of every ṭahāra from ḥadath. doubt_in_condition decides validity when firmness of intention is in doubt, not whether intention is required.
cases.quote: والنية شرط لطهارة الأحداث1 كلها
cases.expected: Intention (niyya) is a condition of every ṭahāra from ḥadath: he intends lifting the ḥadath or ṭahāra for what is permitted only by it.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: «لا يصح الوضوء ولا غيره من العبادات إلا أن ينويه»; agree.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the intention of a masnūn ṭahāra lifts the ḥadath. al-Inṣāf (v01:p144-145) reports two riwāyas and «إحداهما: يرتفع، وهو المذهب»; the other is chosen by Ibn Ḥāmid, al-Qāḍī and Abū al-Khaṭṭāb. tadakhul (qāʿida 18) merges two owed acts of one kind; here there is one wuḍūʾ intended for a recommended end, and whether its niyya reaches the ḥadath is a rule of intention no reading states.
cases.quote: فإن نوى ما تسن له الطهارة كقراءة أو تجديدا مسنونا "ناسيا حدثه" ارتفع
cases.expected: If he intends what ṭahāra is recommended for (reading) or a recommended renewal while forgetting his ḥadath, the ḥadath is lifted.

positions.who: Zād; the riwāya al-Inṣāf calls the madhhab
the other riwāya (Ibn Ḥāmid, al-Qāḍī, Abū al-Khaṭṭāb)

aligned.note: Wuḍūʾ intending the farḍ if in ḥadath, else renewal.
ʿUmda: «وإن نوى بعضها فليس له إلا ما نوى».

cases.note: Leading ruling: a ghusl intended as the masnūn one (Friday, ʿĪd) suffices for the obligatory one, «وكذا عكسه»: two ghusls of one kind and one purpose on one occasion merge into one act (qāʿida 18). al-Inṣāf (v01:p146) gives two wujūh (or riwāyas), its ruling «كالحكم فيما إذا نوى ما تسن له الطهارة، خلافا ومذهبا», where the madhhab is that it suffices; al-Majd: the recommended ghusl does not lift it. al-Iqnāʿ and al-Muntahā state it decisively: on the reading's side; ledger entry. The second ruling, several ḥadaths of one type with one intended («فنوى بطهارته أحدها ارتفع سائرها»), is tadakhul too (same kind, same purpose): the reading decides the whole unit.
cases.quote: وإن نوى غسلا مسنونا أجزأ عن واجب

positions.who: Zād; al-Iqnāʿ, al-Muntahā; the madhhab per al-Inṣāf's referral
the other wajh; al-Majd (lifted by a recommended wuḍūʾ, not by a recommended ghusl)

aligned.note: Two ḥadaths, minor and major, under one greater ṭahāra intending both.
Many causes of one kaffāra: one paid for one of them discharges the rest, as one ḥadath intended lifts the rest.
ʿUmda: «وإن نوى بعضها فليس له إلا ما نوى», of ḥadaths of different kinds with najāsa; Zād's «أحداث توجب وضوءا أو غسلا» are of one kind. No conflict on these facts.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the niyya is due at the first wājib, the tasmiya. Examined: worship_ruled_from_start (an act ruled from its beginning when a sharṭ comes within its time); it does not fix where the intention must fall. Domain rule. Not stated in ʿUmda.
cases.quote: ويجب الإتيان بها عند أول واجبات الطهارة وهو1 التسمية
cases.expected: The intention is due at the first obligatory act of ṭahāra, the tasmiya; it is sunna at the first sunna if before an obligatory one, and keeping it in mind throughout is sunna while keeping its ruling is obligatory.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the order and bounds of wuḍūʾ, a domain description. Within it, «ويغسل الأقطع بقية المفروض» is what partial_capability decides (able to do part, not a mere means: the part is owed), and the ears wiped with the head once agrees with q012.f000.
cases.quote: وصفة الوضوء: أن ينوي ثم يسمي
cases.expected: The description of wuḍūʾ: intention, tasmiya, hands thrice, mouth and nose, the face with its bounds and hair, the arms with the elbows, the whole head with the ears once, the feet with the ankles; the amputee washes what remains of the obligatory part; then the gaze to the sky and the reported words; help and drying are permitted.

aligned.note: ʿUmda gives the same description (face bounds, thick beard combed, light beard washed, elbows and ankles included, the head with the ears, the gaze to the sky); agree. ʿUmda adds the manner of wiping the head front to back and back.
Ears wiped once with the head.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the durations of masḥ, counted from the ḥadath after putting on. A rukhṣa with its periods fixed by the ḥadīth, a domain rule; rukhsa_under_doubt decides only a doubt in its permission. The list continues in p02 (the jabīra and the sharṭ of complete ṭahāra), split at a page break.
cases.quote: يجوز يوما وليلة1 ولمسافر ثلاثة بلياليها
cases.expected: Wiping is permitted a day and a night, and for the traveller three days with their nights, from the ḥadath after putting on a permitted covering of the obligatory part that stays on by itself (khuff, thick socks), a man's ʿimāma with a chin-wrap or a tail, and women's khimār wrapped under the throat, in the minor ḥadath.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: «يوما وليلة للمقيم وثلاثة أيام ولياليهم للمسافر من الحدث إلى مثله», khuffs and thick socks, in the minor ṭahāra; agree.

ʿUmda: the ʿimāma with a tail (dhuʾāba) «ساترة لجميع الرأس», and «إلا أن المرأة لا تمسح على العمامة». Zād also admits a chin-wrapped ʿimāma without a tail and women's khimār: they differ on these coverings.
Ibn Rajab reasons on «وقلنا ابتداء المدة من المسح», the other view of the start; Zād counts from the ḥadath.

cases.note: Second half of the sentence of p01, split at a page break (audit page_break_candidates; p01 ends «في حدث أصغر,»): «وجبيرة …» is one more object of «يجوز … على», and «إذا لبس ذلك بعد كمال الطهارة» is the sharṭ of the whole list. Its rulings: the jabīra not beyond need, even in the major ḥadath, until untied (rule:jabira_wiping); all coverings put on after complete ṭahāra (rule:mash_complete_tahara_condition).

aligned.note: ʿUmda: «ومن شرط المسح على جميع ذلك أن يلبسه على طهارة كاملة ويجوز المسح على الجبيرة إذا لم يتعد بشدها موضع الحاجة إلى أن يحلها»; agree.

cases.note: Leading ruling: a change between travel and residence after wiping began gives the resident's period. A domain rule of the duration. The doubt branch is what rukhsa_under_doubt decides (a rukhṣa needs its permission established; not established: the longer period is not taken), as in q068.f001.
cases.quote: ومن مسح في سفر ثم أقام أو عكس أو شك في ابتدائه فمسح مقيم
cases.expected: Whoever wiped in travel then took up residence, or the reverse, or doubts where it began, wipes as a resident; whoever incurred ḥadath then travelled before wiping wipes as a traveller.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: «ومن مسح مسافرا ثم أقام أو مقيما ثم سافر أتم مسح مقيم»; agree. ʿUmda does not state the doubt or the travel before the first wiping.
Doubt whether the period began in travel or residence.

cases.note: Leading ruling: coverings not eligible for wiping. Domain rule. The upper khuff governing (فالحكم للفوقاني) is examined against tabaa (the lower following the upper), which does not state which of two coverings is the locus.
cases.quote: ولا يمسح قلانس ولا لفافة ولا ما يسقط من القدم أو يرى منه بعضه
cases.expected: No wiping over caps, wrappings, or what falls off the foot or shows part of it; if he put a khuff over a khuff before the ḥadath, the ruling is the upper one's.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: socks «التي تثبت في القدمين»; Zād excludes what falls off or shows part of the foot.

cases.note: Leading ruling: the extent of the wiping. Domain rule; partial_capability concerns inability for part of an act, not a part fixed by the text. Not stated in ʿUmda.
cases.quote: ويمسح أكثر العمامة وظاهر قدم الخف من أصابعه إلى ساقه دون أسفله وعقبه
cases.expected: He wipes most of the ʿimāma and the top of the khuff from the toes to the shin, not its sole or heel, and the whole jabīra.

cases.note: Leading ruling: when part of the farḍ area appears after the ḥadath (the khuff removed or shifted), he restarts the ṭahāra. The question of q143.f001 on its facts: the reading (the wiping stood in place of washing the feet) lets him wash (ghasl) the feet only, a riwāya; Zād, ʿUmda and al-Inṣāf («هذا الصحيح من المذهب») restart: off the reading's side; ledger entry. Not the whole unit: the end of the period (تمت مدته) is a further branch the reading does not reach (rule:mash_period_expiry).
cases.quote: ومتى ظهر بعض محل الفرض "بعد الحدث" أو تمت مدته استأنف الطهارة

positions.who: a riwāya: washing the feet suffices (Ibn Rajab q143.f001)
Zād, ʿUmda; the madhhab per al-Inṣāf: restart the ṭahāra

aligned.note: ʿUmda: «ومتى مسح ثم انقضت المدة أو خلع قبلها بطلت طهارته»; agree.

cases.note: Leading ruling: what exits a passage (sabīl) breaks wuḍūʾ; the enumeration follows. The enumeration of nullifiers is a domain rule. Within it, sleep breaks wuḍūʾ as the presumptive locus of ḥadath (q159.f016, asl_zahir), and touching hair, teeth or nails does not (q002.f000, hair_detached). The list continues in p02 (page break).
cases.quote: ينقض ما خرج من سبيل
cases.expected: Wuḍūʾ is broken by what exits a passage, by urine, excrement or much najis matter from the rest of the body, by loss of reason except light sleep of one sitting or standing, by touching the penis or the vulva with the hand, by touching with desire as listed, and by touching the anus; not by touching hair, teeth or nails.

aligned.note: Deep sleep breaks wuḍūʾ; Zād excepts light sleep «من قاعد وقائم».
Touching hair or nail with desire does not break wuḍūʾ; Zād: «لا مس شعر».

ʿUmda: «هي سبعة: الخارج من السبيلين والخارج النجس من غيرهما إذا فحش وزوال العقل إلا النوم اليسير جالسا أو قائما ولمس الذكر بيده ولمس امرأة» (with desire, «بشهوة», in the next record); agree on these. ʿUmda counts apostasy (ridda) and not washing the dead; Zād adds the vulva, the anus and the washing of the dead.

cases.note: Second half of the enumeration of p01, split at a page break (audit page_break_candidates; p01 ends «وظفر»): «وأمرد …» continues «لا مس …». Its rulings: no nullification by touching a beardless youth, through a barrier, or for the one touched; ghusl of the dead and eating camel meat break wuḍūʾ (rule:wudu_nullifiers).

aligned.note: ʿUmda: camel meat breaks wuḍūʾ («وأكل لحم الإبل»); agree. ʿUmda does not count washing the dead.

cases.note: A general domain rule (ḍābiṭ) of the nullifiers. tadakhul decides whether one ṭahāra discharges both, not whether a sabab of ghusl is also a sabab of wuḍūʾ.
cases.quote: وكل ما أوجب غسلا أوجب الوضوء إلا الموت
cases.expected: Whatever makes ghusl obligatory makes wuḍūʾ obligatory, except death.

aligned.note: ʿUmda enumerates seven nullifiers, with apostasy, and gives no such rule.

cases.note: Leading ruling: certain of ṭahāra and doubting ḥadath, or the reverse: build on certainty. q159.f007 on its facts («وكذلك لو تيقن حدثا … فإنه يبني على الأصل»): the ẓāhir does not prevail over the aṣl. Not the whole unit: certain of both with the earlier unknown, he takes the opposite of his state before them (rule:unknown_order_of_tahara_and_hadath).
cases.quote: ومن تيقن الطهارة وشك في الحدث أو بالعكس بنى على اليقين

aligned.note: ʿUmda: «ومن تيقن الطهارة وشك في الحدث أو تيقن الحدث وشك ف الطهارة فهو على ما تيقن منهما»; agree. ʿUmda does not state the case of both certain.

cases.note: What ḥadath forbids: a domain rule. prohibited_worship decides the validity of a prohibited act, not what the ḥadath prohibits.
cases.quote: ويحرم على المحدث مس المصحف والصلاة والطواف
cases.expected: Touching the muṣḥaf, prayer and ṭawāf are forbidden to one in ḥadath.

aligned.note: ʿUmda: menstruation forbids prayer, ṭawāf and touching the muṣḥaf, among ten.
ʿUmda: ṭahāra from ḥadath is the first condition of prayer.
